Insulin chiefly recruits GLUT4 in skeletal muscle and adipose; many tissues use insulin-independent GLUTs
GLUT4 vesicles translocate to the plasma membrane
They lack mitochondria and depend entirely on glycolysis

glucose-transport-glycolysis.explanation: Brain and RBC glucose uptake must continue even when insulin is low.

glucose-transport-glycolysis.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Glucose Transport & Glycolysis”?
glucose-transport-glycolysis.explanation: Glycolysis is a key energy source for skeletal muscle.

pentose-fructose-galactose.stem: An infant develops jaundice, hepatomegaly, cataracts, and E. coli sepsis after milk feeding. Which enzyme is deficient?
pentose-fructose-galactose.explanation: The multisystem neonatal presentation is classic galactosemia from GALT deficiency.

pentose-fructose-galactose.stem: Regarding fructose disorders — which is correct?

options.text: All fructose enzyme defects cause severe fasting hypoglycemia
Aldolase B deficiency is severe; fructokinase deficiency causes benign essential fructosuria
Splenic removal of Heinz-body precipitates in G6PD deficiency
Aldolase B deficiency traps phosphate as fructose-1-phosphate

pentose-fructose-galactose.explanation: Phosphate trapping and inhibition of glycogenolysis/gluconeogenesis occur in aldolase B deficiency.

pentose-fructose-galactose.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Pentose Phosphate, Fructose & Galactose Pathways”?
pentose-fructose-galactose.explanation: Clinical implications of G6PD deficiency relate to oxidative stress and hemolysis.

pentose-fructose-galactose.stem: Which should you review before “Pentose Phosphate, Fructose & Galactose Pathways”?
pentose-fructose-galactose.explanation: Understanding G6PD is crucial for grasping oxidative hemolysis in RBCs.

glycogen-synthesis-breakdown.stem: Why can liver glycogen maintain blood glucose while muscle glycogen cannot?
glycogen-synthesis-breakdown.explanation: Liver expresses glucose-6-phosphatase and can release free glucose; skeletal muscle does not.

glycogen-synthesis-breakdown.stem: Regarding liver versus muscle glycogen — which is correct?

options.text: Muscle glycogen directly raises blood glucose
Muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase, so its glycogen is reserved for local glycolysis
Failure of hepatic free-glucose release in glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency

glycogen-synthesis-breakdown.explanation: Only tissues with glucose-6-phosphatase can release free glucose.

glycogen-synthesis-breakdown.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Glycogen Synthesis, Breakdown & Hormonal Control”?

options.text: Hormonal Control of Volume & Water Balance

glycogen-synthesis-breakdown.explanation: Hormonal control is a key aspect of glycogen metabolism.

gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.stem: Which substrate contributes carbon to net hepatic gluconeogenesis during fasting?
gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.explanation: Glycerol enters as DHAP. Even-chain fatty acids, leucine, and ketone bodies do not yield net glucose.

gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.stem: Regarding gluconeogenic substrate — which is correct?

options.text: Acetyl-CoA from even-chain fatty acids can make net glucose
Even-chain acetyl-CoA cannot produce net glucose in humans
High NADH blocks lactate/alanine entry into gluconeogenesis
It transports both carbon and amino nitrogen to liver

gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.explanation: PDH is irreversible and both acetyl carbons are lost as CO₂ during TCA cycling.

gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Gluconeogenesis, Cori Cycle & Glucose–Alanine Cycle”?
gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.explanation: Insulin sensitizers affect glucose metabolism and gluconeogenesis.

gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.stem: Which should you review before “Gluconeogenesis, Cori Cycle & Glucose–Alanine Cycle”?
gluconeogenesis-cori-alanine.explanation: Understanding glucose homeostasis is essential for grasping gluconeogenesis.

blood-glucose-homeostasis.stem: Which process becomes the dominant source of blood glucose as an overnight fast continues and hepatic glycogen declines?
blood-glucose-homeostasis.explanation: Gluconeogenesis increases progressively and becomes dominant as the finite liver glycogen store is depleted.

blood-glucose-homeostasis.stem: Regarding glucagon target tissue — which is correct?

options.text: Glucagon directly activates skeletal-muscle glycogen phosphorylase
Glucagon acts mainly on liver; skeletal muscle responds to epinephrine and contraction signals
Insulin-mediated disposal plus suppression of hepatic glucose production
Brain fuel shortage plus sympathoadrenal counter-regulation

blood-glucose-homeostasis.explanation: Skeletal muscle lacks a meaningful glucagon response and keeps its glycogen for local use.

blood-glucose-homeostasis.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Blood-Glucose Homeostasis”?
blood-glucose-homeostasis.explanation: Brain metabolism is influenced by blood glucose levels.

blood-glucose-homeostasis.stem: Which should you review before “Blood-Glucose Homeostasis”?
blood-glucose-homeostasis.explanation: Gluconeogenesis is a key process in blood-glucose homeostasis.

amino-nitrogen-handling.stem: Which vitamin-derived cofactor is required by aminotransferases?
amino-nitrogen-handling.explanation: Pyridoxal phosphate, derived from vitamin B6, carries amino groups during transamination.

amino-nitrogen-handling.stem: Regarding meaning of aminotransferase elevation — which is correct?

options.text: High ALT proves that hepatic protein synthesis is increased
High ALT usually reflects enzyme leakage from injured hepatocytes
Hepatocellular leakage of a relatively liver-enriched enzyme

amino-nitrogen-handling.explanation: Aminotransferases are injury markers, not direct liver-function tests.

amino-nitrogen-handling.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Amino-Acid Nitrogen Handling”?

options.text: Renal Handling of Ca²⁺, PO₄, Mg²⁺, Cl⁻ & Urate

amino-nitrogen-handling.explanation: Some overlap in metabolic pathways but less direct relevance.

urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.stem: A boy has hyperammonemia, low BUN, respiratory alkalosis, and increased urine orotic acid. Which enzyme is deficient?
urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.explanation: The combination of hyperammonemia and high orotic acid is classic for X-linked OTC deficiency.

urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.stem: Regarding otc versus ump-synthase deficiency — which is correct?

options.text: High orotic acid always causes megaloblastic anemia
OTC deficiency causes hyperammonemia without megaloblastic anemia; UMP-synthase deficiency causes megaloblastic anemia without hyperammonemia
Ammonia cannot be incorporated into urea
Mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate spills into pyrimidine synthesis in OTC deficiency

urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.explanation: The same metabolite rises through different pathway defects.

urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Urea Cycle & Hyperammonemia”?
urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.explanation: Insulin therapy may be relevant in metabolic contexts involving amino acids.

urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.stem: Which should you review before “Urea Cycle & Hyperammonemia”?
urea-cycle-hyperammonemia.explanation: Understanding nitrogen handling is crucial for grasping urea cycle function.

amino-carbon-skeleton-disorders.stem: Which amino acids are exclusively ketogenic?
amino-carbon-skeleton-disorders.explanation: Leucine and lysine are the only amino acids whose carbon skeletons are exclusively ketogenic.

amino-carbon-skeleton-disorders.stem: Regarding maternal pku — which is correct?

options.text: Only a fetus who inherits PKU is at risk
Poorly controlled maternal phenylalanine is teratogenic even when the fetus has normal PAH genes
Phenylalanine accumulation and reduced tyrosine-derived melanin in PKU
Accumulated branched-chain amino/keto acids in MSUD

amino-carbon-skeleton-disorders.explanation: The fetal exposure is determined by maternal metabolic control.

amino-carbon-skeleton-disorders.stem: Which should you review before “Amino-Acid Carbon Skeletons & Inborn Errors”?
amino-carbon-skeleton-disorders.explanation: Understanding nitrogen handling is essential for amino acid metabolism.

one-carbon-carriers.stem: Which finding most strongly favors vitamin B₁₂ deficiency over isolated folate deficiency?
one-carbon-carriers.explanation: Both deficiencies cause megaloblastosis and high homocysteine, but methylmalonic acid rises in B₁₂ deficiency.

one-carbon-carriers.stem: Regarding folate rescue — which is correct?

options.text: Folate alone fully treats any megaloblastic anemia
Folate can normalize the blood count in B₁₂ deficiency but does not prevent neurologic injury
Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency impairs DNA synthesis and myelin metabolism

one-carbon-carriers.explanation: The hematologic and neurologic consequences of B₁₂ deficiency can dissociate.

one-carbon-carriers.stem: Which is a clinical application of “One-Carbon Carriers: THF, B₁₂ & SAM (SDL)”?
one-carbon-carriers.explanation: Clinical implications of B₁₂ and folate absorption are vital for understanding deficiencies.

one-carbon-carriers.stem: Which should you review before “One-Carbon Carriers: THF, B₁₂ & SAM (SDL)”?
one-carbon-carriers.explanation: Understanding vitamin absorption is crucial for grasping B₁₂ and folate metabolism.

amino-acid-derived-products.stem: Which three amino acids form glutathione?
Regarding glutathione regeneration — which is correct?

options.text: Glutathione peroxidase consumes GSH; glutathione reductase uses NADPH to regenerate GSH
RBC proteins and membranes lose peroxide protection

amino-acid-derived-products.explanation: NADPH from the pentose phosphate pathway maintains the antioxidant pool.

amino-acid-derived-products.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Amino-Acid-Derived Molecules”?
amino-acid-derived-products.explanation: Adrenal androgens are derived from amino acids, linking basic science to clinical application.

tag-storage-mobilization.stem: Where does glycerol released from adipose TAG travel for metabolism during fasting?

options.text: Directly into ketone bodies in blood

tag-storage-mobilization.explanation: Adipose has little glycerol kinase, so glycerol travels to liver for gluconeogenesis or TAG synthesis.

tag-storage-mobilization.stem: Regarding lipoprotein lipase versus hormone-sensitive lipase — which is correct?

options.text: Hormone-sensitive lipase hydrolyzes TAG inside circulating chylomicrons
LPL acts on circulating chylomicron/VLDL TAG; adipocyte ATGL/HSL mobilize stored TAG
Adipose lipolysis releases stored acyl chains
Adipose has low glycerol kinase activity

tag-storage-mobilization.explanation: The enzymes act in different compartments and respond differently to insulin.

tag-storage-mobilization.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Triacylglycerol Storage & Mobilization”?

fatty-acid-synthesis-eicosanoids.stem: Which metabolite directly inhibits CPT I during active fatty-acid synthesis?
fatty-acid-synthesis-eicosanoids.explanation: ACC produces malonyl-CoA, which prevents mitochondrial entry of long-chain fatty acyl-CoA through CPT I.

fatty-acid-synthesis-eicosanoids.stem: Regarding synthesis versus oxidation — which is correct?

options.text: Fatty-acid synthesis and β-oxidation run together after insulin
Malonyl-CoA promotes synthesis while inhibiting CPT I, preventing simultaneous long-chain β-oxidation
Insulin activates ACC and simultaneously suppresses mitochondrial fatty-acid entry
Impaired barrier lipids and eicosanoid precursors

fatty-acid-synthesis-eicosanoids.explanation: Reciprocal regulation avoids a futile cycle.

beta-oxidation-carnitine.stem: A toddler becomes lethargic after an overnight fast and has hypoglycemia with very low ketones. Which pathway is most likely impaired?
beta-oxidation-carnitine.explanation: Hypoketotic hypoglycemia after fasting is the classic presentation of MCAD or another fatty-acid oxidation defect.

beta-oxidation-carnitine.stem: Regarding fatty-acid oxidation presentation — which is correct?

options.text: A fasting FA-oxidation defect should cause marked ketosis
It produces hypoketotic hypoglycemia because acetyl-CoA for ketone synthesis is unavailable
Fatty-acid oxidation cannot supply ATP or acetyl-CoA for ketogenesis/gluconeogenesis
Compensatory ω-oxidation when β-oxidation is impaired

beta-oxidation-carnitine.explanation: Failure to use fat removes both an alternate fuel and a driver of gluconeogenesis.

ketone-body-metabolism.stem: Why can the liver synthesize but not utilize ketone bodies?
ketone-body-metabolism.explanation: Hepatocytes lack thiophorase (succinyl-CoA:acetoacetate CoA transferase), required for ketolysis.

ketone-body-metabolism.stem: Regarding ketone use — which is correct?

options.text: Liver uses ketones as soon as it produces them
Liver exports ketones because it lacks thiophorase; peripheral mitochondria consume them
Acetone odor plus respiratory compensation for ketoacidosis
Nitroprusside detects acetoacetate better than β-hydroxybutyrate

ketone-body-metabolism.explanation: This preserves ketones as a circulating fuel during fasting.

ketone-body-metabolism.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Ketogenesis, Ketolysis & Ketoacidosis”?
ketone-body-metabolism.explanation: Insulin therapy is crucial in managing conditions like DKA related to ketogenesis.

ketone-body-metabolism.stem: Which should you review before “Ketogenesis, Ketolysis & Ketoacidosis”?
ketone-body-metabolism.explanation: Understanding β-oxidation is crucial for grasping ketogenesis.

cholesterol-bile-steroids.stem: What is the rate-limiting enzyme in bile-acid synthesis from cholesterol?
cholesterol-bile-steroids.explanation: CYP7A1 (cholesterol 7α-hydroxylase) controls conversion of cholesterol into primary bile acids.

cholesterol-bile-steroids.stem: Regarding cytosolic hmg-coa fate — which is correct?

options.text: Cytosolic HMG-CoA feeds cholesterol synthesis; mitochondrial HMG-CoA feeds ketogenesis
Competitive HMG-CoA reductase inhibition lowers hepatic cholesterol
Reduced enterohepatic bile-salt pool impairs micelle formation

cholesterol-bile-steroids.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Cholesterol, Bile Acids & Steroids (SDL)”?
cholesterol-bile-steroids.explanation: Clinical implications of bile acid synthesis are directly linked to cholesterol metabolism.

cholesterol-bile-steroids.stem: Which should you review before “Cholesterol, Bile Acids & Steroids (SDL)”?

options.text: Fatty-Acid Synthesis, Essential Fatty Acids & Eicosanoids

cholesterol-bile-steroids.explanation: Understanding fatty acid synthesis is foundational for lipid metabolism.

lipoproteins-atherogenesis.stem: Which apolipoprotein activates lipoprotein lipase on capillary endothelium?
lipoproteins-atherogenesis.explanation: ApoC-II activates LPL, allowing hydrolysis of TAG in chylomicrons and VLDL.

lipoproteins-atherogenesis.stem: Regarding apolipoprotein identity — which is correct?

options.text: ApoB-48 binds the LDL receptor on peripheral cells
ApoB-100 is the LDL-receptor ligand; apoB-48 is the structural protein of chylomicrons
Familial hypercholesterolemia impairs LDL-receptor pathway clearance
Severe chylomicronemia from impaired LPL activity

lipoproteins-atherogenesis.explanation: RNA editing creates the shorter intestinal apoB-48 protein.

lipoproteins-atherogenesis.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Lipoproteins & Atherogenesis (SDL)”?
lipoproteins-atherogenesis.explanation: Clinical implications of lipoprotein metabolism in cardiovascular disease.

alternative-fatty-acid-oxidation.stem: Odd-chain fatty-acid oxidation produces which gluconeogenic TCA intermediate?
alternative-fatty-acid-oxidation.explanation: The terminal propionyl-CoA is converted through methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA.

alternative-fatty-acid-oxidation.stem: Regarding peroxisomal energy yield — which is correct?

options.text: Peroxisomal first-step FADH2 feeds the ETC and makes ATP
Peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase passes electrons directly to oxygen, producing hydrogen peroxide
ABCD1-related VLCFA accumulation in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy

alternative-fatty-acid-oxidation.explanation: Peroxisomes shorten VLCFAs but do not conserve that first oxidation energy as ATP.

alternative-fatty-acid-oxidation.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Peroxisomal, α-, ω- & Odd-Chain Fatty-Acid Oxidation”?

organ-specific-fuel-metabolism.stem: Which tissue necessarily converts glucose to lactate even in well-oxygenated blood?
organ-specific-fuel-metabolism.explanation: Erythrocytes lack mitochondria, so glycolytic pyruvate must be reduced to lactate to regenerate NAD⁺.

organ-specific-fuel-metabolism.stem: Regarding brain fuel in starvation — which is correct?

options.text: The brain switches mainly to free fatty acids
The brain uses ketone bodies while retaining some glucose requirement
No mitochondria for PDH, TCA, or oxidative phosphorylation
Adaptation reduces glucose demand and muscle-protein loss

organ-specific-fuel-metabolism.explanation: Long-chain fatty acids cross the blood–brain barrier poorly, whereas ketones are water-soluble.

fed-fasting-starvation.stem: What adaptation most directly reduces muscle-protein loss during prolonged starvation?
fed-fasting-starvation.explanation: Brain ketone use lowers its glucose demand, so fewer amino acids are required for gluconeogenesis.

fed-fasting-starvation.stem: Regarding sequence of fasting fuels — which is correct?

options.text: Gluconeogenesis begins only after glycogen is completely gone
Gluconeogenesis begins early and increases as glycogenolysis declines
Brain ketone adaptation reduces amino-acid demand for gluconeogenesis
Low insulin/high glucagon promotes hepatic ketogenesis

fed-fasting-starvation.explanation: Pathways overlap; the dominant contribution shifts gradually.

fed-fasting-starvation.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Fed, Fasting & Starvation States”?
fed-fasting-starvation.explanation: Understanding metabolic acidosis can relate to fasting and starvation states.

exercise-stress-fuel-integration.stem: Which fuel system predominates during the first few seconds of maximal exercise?
exercise-stress-fuel-integration.explanation: Stored ATP and phosphocreatine provide the fastest energy before glycolytic and oxidative pathways ramp up.

exercise-stress-fuel-integration.stem: Regarding glut4 regulation — which is correct?

options.text: Skeletal muscle can recruit GLUT4 only through insulin
Muscle contraction independently recruits GLUT4, and its effect adds to insulin
Cori cycling recycles carbon while liver bears the ATP cost

exercise-stress-fuel-integration.explanation: This explains glucose uptake during exercise even when insulin is low.

exercise-stress-fuel-integration.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Exercise, Stress Hormones & Fuel Integration”?

metabolic-junction-points.stem: Which central metabolite can enter fatty-acid synthesis, cholesterol synthesis, ketogenesis, or the TCA cycle but cannot yield net glucose?
metabolic-junction-points.explanation: Acetyl-CoA is a central oxidative and biosynthetic junction, but humans cannot convert it to net glucose.

metabolic-junction-points.stem: Regarding carbon tracing — which is correct?

options.text: Any substrate that becomes acetyl-CoA is glucogenic
Acetyl-CoA is oxidizable and ketogenic/lipogenic, but it does not produce net glucose in humans
ALT and LDH connect amino-acid and anaerobic carbon to the pyruvate junction
No net human pathway from acetyl-CoA to oxaloacetate/glucose

metabolic-junction-points.explanation: Entry into TCA does not equal net oxaloacetate gain.

acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.stem: Which finding best indicates worsening hepatic function in acetaminophen toxicity?
acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.explanation: INR reflects hepatic synthetic failure; aminotransferases measure injury and may fall as viable hepatocytes are lost.

acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.stem: Regarding nomogram use — which is correct?

options.text: Plot any acetaminophen concentration regardless of timing or ingestion pattern
Use the nomogram only for a known-time, single acute ingestion
Loss of viable hepatocytes can lower enzyme release while synthetic failure worsens

acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.explanation: Repeated supratherapeutic ingestion and unknown-time cases require clinical and laboratory judgment instead.

acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Acetaminophen Overdose: Clinical & Laboratory Pattern”?

options.text: Ascending Cholangitis, Bile Flow & Fat-Soluble Vitamins

acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.explanation: Understanding opioid toxicity can provide insights into managing overdose scenarios.

acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.stem: Which should you review before “Acetaminophen Overdose: Clinical & Laboratory Pattern”?

options.text: Ascending Cholangitis, Bile Flow & Fat-Soluble Vitamins

acetaminophen-overdose-pattern.explanation: Understanding NAPQI and glutathione depletion is crucial for acetaminophen toxicity.

napqi-glutathione-nac.stem: What is the principal early protective action of N-acetylcysteine in acetaminophen overdose?
napqi-glutathione-nac.explanation: NAC provides cysteine for glutathione synthesis, restoring detoxification of NAPQI.

napqi-glutathione-nac.stem: Regarding why nac still helps late — which is correct?

options.text: NAC has no value once AST/ALT are elevated
NAC can still improve antioxidant capacity and outcomes in established acetaminophen liver injury
Zone 3 has high CYP2E1 activity and vulnerability to oxidative injury
Lower glutathione reserve and/or CYP2E1 induction increases vulnerability

napqi-glutathione-nac.explanation: Its benefits extend beyond preventing the first NAPQI-protein bond.

napqi-glutathione-nac.stem: Which is a clinical application of “NAPQI, Glutathione Depletion & N-Acetylcysteine”?

options.text: Ascending Cholangitis, Bile Flow & Fat-Soluble Vitamins

napqi-glutathione-nac.stem: Which should you review before “NAPQI, Glutathione Depletion & N-Acetylcysteine”?

options.text: Ascending Cholangitis, Bile Flow & Fat-Soluble Vitamins

napqi-glutathione-nac.explanation: Understanding acetaminophen overdose is crucial for grasping NAPQI's role.

cholestatic-lab-pattern.stem: Which laboratory pattern most strongly supports extrahepatic biliary obstruction?

options.text: AST and ALT elevation with normal ALP
Disproportionate ALP/GGT elevation with direct hyperbilirubinemia

cholestatic-lab-pattern.explanation: A cholestatic enzyme pattern plus conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is typical of bile-flow obstruction.

cholestatic-lab-pattern.stem: Regarding bilirubin in urine — which is correct?

options.text: Only conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble enough to appear in urine

vitamin-absorption.explanation: Folate and B12 are critical for one-carbon metabolism.

mineral-water-absorption.stem: Which hormone decreases intestinal iron absorption by promoting ferroportin degradation?
mineral-water-absorption.explanation: Hepcidin reduces plasma iron entry by degrading the exporter ferroportin.

mineral-water-absorption.stem: Regarding iron regulation — which is correct?

options.text: Hepcidin increases ferroportin to improve iron absorption
Hepcidin binds ferroportin and promotes its internalization and degradation
Inflammatory hepcidin degrades enterocyte ferroportin and traps iron
SGLT1-coupled Na⁺ uptake drives water absorption

mineral-water-absorption.explanation: This reduces iron export from enterocytes and macrophages into plasma.

mineral-water-absorption.stem: Which should you review before “Mineral, Electrolyte & Water Absorption”?

options.text: Stomach Regions, Gastric Pits & Gland Cells

mineral-water-absorption.explanation: Understanding fluid compartments is essential for grasping electrolyte distribution.

bile-composition-acid-synthesis.stem: What is the rate-limiting enzyme in the classic hepatic bile-acid synthesis pathway?
bile-composition-acid-synthesis.explanation: CYP7A1 catalyzes the rate-limiting hydroxylation in conversion of cholesterol to primary bile acids.

bile-composition-acid-synthesis.stem: Regarding bile function — which is correct?

options.text: Bile salts emulsify lipid and form micelles; pancreatic lipase performs hydrolysis
Insufficient luminal bile salts impair mixed-micelle formation
Cholesterol exceeds the solubilizing capacity of bile salts and phospholipids

bile-composition-acid-synthesis.explanation: Bile salts are physical detergents, not digestive enzymes.

bile-composition-acid-synthesis.stem: Which should you review before “Bile Composition & Bile Acid Synthesis”?

options.text: Stomach Regions, Gastric Pits & Gland Cells

bile-composition-acid-synthesis.explanation: Understanding cholesterol is essential for grasping bile acid synthesis.

enterohepatic-bile-circulation.stem: Where does active reabsorption of most bile salts occur?
enterohepatic-bile-circulation.explanation: Terminal-ileal ASBT actively reclaims most bile salts for portal return to the liver.

enterohepatic-bile-circulation.stem: Regarding ileal bile-acid loss — which is correct?

options.text: A bile-acid sequestrant always improves symptoms after any ileal resection
It may help excess colonic bile acids but worsen steatorrhea when the bile-salt pool is profoundly depleted
Unabsorbed bile acids stimulate colonic electrolyte and water secretion
Bile-salt pool depletion prevents adequate micelle formation

enterohepatic-bile-circulation.explanation: The effect depends on whether excess colonic bile acid or inadequate micellar bile acid dominates.

enterohepatic-bile-circulation.stem: Which should you review before “Enterohepatic Circulation of Bile Salts”?

options.text: Stomach Regions, Gastric Pits & Gland Cells

enterohepatic-bile-circulation.explanation: Understanding lipid digestion is essential for grasping bile salt function.

bile-formation-gallbladder-emptying.stem: Which hormone most directly contracts the gallbladder after a fatty meal?
bile-formation-gallbladder-emptying.explanation: CCK released from duodenal I cells contracts the gallbladder and promotes sphincter of Oddi relaxation.

bile-formation-gallbladder-emptying.stem: Regarding biliary hormonal control — which is correct?

options.text: Secretin is the principal trigger for gallbladder contraction
CCK contracts the gallbladder; secretin stimulates bicarbonate-rich ductal secretion
Duodenal CCK coordinates gallbladder and sphincter of Oddi
Conjugated bilirubin reaches urine rather than intestine, reducing stercobilin formation

bile-formation-gallbladder-emptying.explanation: The two hormones coordinate distinct but complementary biliary responses.

hrp1-female-pelvis-neurovascular.stem: Which nerves carry parasympathetic fibers to pelvic viscera?
hrp1-female-pelvis-neurovascular.explanation: Pelvic splanchnic nerves from S2–S4 provide parasympathetic pelvic outflow.

hrp1-female-pelvis-neurovascular.stem: Regarding pelvic innervation — which is correct?

options.text: The pudendal nerve provides parasympathetic supply to pelvic organs
Pudendal is somatic; pelvic splanchnics carry parasympathetics
Pudendal or sacral somatic injury affects S2–S4 functions
Hypogastric plexus pathways coordinate visceral activity

hrp1-female-pelvis-neurovascular.explanation: Both arise from S2–S4 but serve different functional systems.

hrp1-female-pelvis-neurovascular.stem: Which should you review before “Female Pelvis, Fascia, Nerves & Vessels”?
hrp1-female-pelvis-neurovascular.explanation: Understanding of vascular and nerve anatomy is relevant.

hrp1-uterus-vagina-support.stem: Which structure passes inferior to the uterine artery near the cervix?
hrp1-uterus-vagina-support.explanation: The ureter passes beneath the uterine artery—water under the bridge.

hrp1-uterus-vagina-support.stem: Regarding uterine support — which is correct?

options.text: Broad ligament is the principal load-bearing uterine support
Pelvic floor and cardinal/uterosacral supports carry the major load
Ureter passes immediately inferior to the artery
Failure of pelvic floor and apical fascial support permits descent

hrp1-uterus-vagina-support.explanation: Broad ligament is a peritoneal fold rather than a strong suspensory ligament.

hrp1-uterus-vagina-support.stem: Which should you review before “Uterus, Vagina & Pelvic Support”?

options.text: Infratemporal Fossa: Mandibular Nerve & Maxillary Artery

hrp1-uterus-vagina-support.explanation: Basic understanding of anatomical structures is beneficial.

hrp1-uterine-tube-ovary-lymph.stem: Where does fertilization most commonly occur?
hrp1-uterine-tube-ovary-lymph.explanation: The ampulla is the widest tubal segment and the usual site of fertilization.

hrp1-uterine-tube-ovary-lymph.stem: Regarding ovarian lymph — which is correct?

options.text: Ovary drains mainly to superficial inguinal nodes
Ovarian lymph follows gonadal vessels to para-aortic nodes
Ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy causes hemoperitoneum
Torsion impairs venous then arterial flow

hrp1-uterine-tube-ovary-lymph.explanation: The ovary retains the drainage pattern of its upper abdominal embryologic origin.

hrp1-uterine-tube-ovary-lymph.stem: Which should you review before “Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy”?
hrp1-uterine-tube-ovary-lymph.explanation: Understanding gametogenesis is essential for grasping ovarian function.

hrp1-ovarian-follicle-histology.stem: Which structure directly surrounds the oocyte at ovulation?
hrp1-ovarian-follicle-histology.explanation: The corona radiata is the innermost cumulus granulosa layer traveling with the secondary oocyte.

hrp1-ovarian-follicle-histology.stem: Regarding oocyte stage — which is correct?

options.text: A mature follicle normally contains a completed ovum before the LH surge
The primary oocyte completes meiosis I around the LH surge and ovulates as a secondary oocyte
Follicular atresia affects most recruited follicles

hrp1-ovarian-follicle-histology.explanation: Meiosis II completes only after fertilization.

hrp1-ovulation-corpus-luteum-histology.stem: Which hormone rescues the corpus luteum in early pregnancy?
hrp1-ovulation-corpus-luteum-histology.explanation: Trophoblastic hCG stimulates LH receptors on luteal cells.

hrp1-ovulation-corpus-luteum-histology.stem: Regarding early pregnancy support — which is correct?

options.text: Placental progesterone fully replaces corpus luteum immediately at fertilization
hCG maintains the corpus luteum until placental steroid production is sufficient
Regressed corpus luteum forms corpus albicans

hrp1-ovulation-corpus-luteum-histology.explanation: Early implantation depends on continued luteal progesterone.

hrp1-ovulation-corpus-luteum-histology.stem: Which should you review before “Ovulation, Corpus Luteum & Follicular Atresia”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-ovulation-corpus-luteum-histology.explanation: Understanding metabolic effects can provide context for hormonal regulation.

hrp1-oviduct-uterus-cycle-histology.stem: Which hormone drives secretory transformation of endometrial glands?
hrp1-oviduct-uterus-cycle-histology.explanation: Postovulatory progesterone converts proliferative endometrium into an implantation-ready secretory state.

hrp1-oviduct-uterus-cycle-histology.stem: Regarding menstrual regeneration — which is correct?

options.text: The entire endometrium is shed every month
The functional layer sheds; basal layer remains to regenerate it

hrp1-oviduct-uterus-cycle-histology.explanation: Deep basal glands and stroma survive menstruation.

hrp1-cervix-vagina-histology.stem: Which cervical region is the major target of HPV-related screening?
hrp1-cervix-vagina-histology.explanation: The transformation zone at the squamocolumnar junction is the common site of cervical dysplasia.

hrp1-cervix-vagina-histology.stem: Regarding vaginal histology — which is correct?

options.text: Vaginal lubrication comes from numerous mucosal glands
Transformation zone adapts to vaginal environment and is vulnerable to HPV dysplasia
Lubrication derives from cervical mucus, transudate, and vestibular glands

hrp1-cervix-vagina-histology.explanation: Fluid comes mainly from transudation and nearby cervical/vestibular sources.

hrp1-cervix-vagina-histology.stem: Which should you review before “Cervix, Transformation Zone & Vagina Histology”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-cervix-vagina-histology.explanation: Glycogen metabolism is crucial for vaginal health and lactobacilli function.

hrp1-breast-gross-lymphatic-anatomy.stem: Most lymph from the breast drains initially toward which nodes?
hrp1-breast-gross-lymphatic-anatomy.explanation: Axillary nodes receive most breast lymph, especially from lateral quadrants.

hrp1-breast-gross-lymphatic-anatomy.stem: Regarding axillary nerve injury — which is correct?

options.text: Winged scapula reflects thoracodorsal nerve injury
It reflects long thoracic nerve injury
Long thoracic nerve injury denervates serratus anterior

hrp1-breast-gross-lymphatic-anatomy.explanation: Long thoracic nerve supplies serratus anterior, which anchors scapula to thoracic wall.

hrp1-breast-gross-lymphatic-anatomy.stem: Which should you review before “Breast Gross Anatomy, Blood Supply & Lymphatics”?

options.text: BRCA1, Homologous Recombination & Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-breast-gross-lymphatic-anatomy.explanation: Understanding BRCA1 is crucial for breast cancer pathology.

hrp1-mammary-gland-histology.stem: Which cells contract to eject milk from mammary alveoli?
hrp1-mammary-gland-histology.explanation: Oxytocin stimulates myoepithelial cells surrounding alveoli and small ducts.

hrp1-mammary-gland-histology.stem: Regarding milk secretion — which is correct?

options.text: Milk fat and protein use identical secretory mechanisms
Protein uses merocrine exocytosis; lipid buds apically
Active lactating gland dominates over stroma

hrp1-mammary-gland-histology.explanation: Different milk components leave luminal cells by distinct routes.

hrp1-placenta-villi-barrier-circulation.stem: What distinguishes a tertiary chorionic villus?
hrp1-placenta-villi-barrier-circulation.explanation: Tertiary villi contain fetal blood vessels within their mesenchymal cores.

hrp1-placenta-villi-barrier-circulation.stem: Regarding placental circulation — which is correct?

options.text: Maternal and fetal blood normally mix freely in intervillous space
They remain separated by the placental barrier
Aggregated syncytiotrophoblast nuclei reflect villous maturation

hrp1-placenta-villi-barrier-circulation.explanation: Exchange occurs across trophoblast and fetal capillary layers, not through a shared vessel.

hrp1-placenta-villi-barrier-circulation.stem: Which should you review before “Placental Villi, Barrier & Maternal–Fetal Circulation”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-placenta-villi-barrier-circulation.explanation: Fundamental understanding of placental structure and function.

hrp1-testis-epididymis-vas-anatomy.stem: Testicular lymph drains primarily to which nodes?
hrp1-testis-epididymis-vas-anatomy.explanation: Testicular lymph follows gonadal vessels to lumbar/para-aortic nodes.

hrp1-testis-epididymis-vas-anatomy.stem: Regarding male genital lymph — which is correct?

options.text: Testis and scrotal skin share superficial inguinal drainage
Testis drains para-aortic; scrotum drains superficial inguinal
Spermatic-cord torsion compromises venous then arterial flow
Varicocele dilates pampiniform veins, commonly on left

hrp1-testis-epididymis-vas-anatomy.explanation: Testis descends from posterior abdominal wall and retains its original vessels and lymphatics.

hrp1-male-accessory-glands-anatomy.stem: The ejaculatory duct is formed by union of the vas deferens with which duct?
hrp1-male-accessory-glands-anatomy.explanation: The ampulla of vas joins the duct of seminal vesicle to form the ejaculatory duct.

hrp1-male-accessory-glands-anatomy.stem: Regarding prostatic zones — which is correct?

options.text: BPH and most prostate cancers arise in the same zone
BPH favors transition zone; carcinoma commonly arises peripherally
Peripheral-zone carcinoma may be palpable on rectal examination

hrp1-male-accessory-glands-anatomy.explanation: This explains early urinary obstruction in BPH and rectal palpability of many cancers.

hrp1-male-accessory-glands-anatomy.stem: Which should you review before “Seminal Vesicles, Ejaculatory Ducts, Prostate & Bulbourethral Glands”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-male-accessory-glands-anatomy.explanation: Understanding transport mechanisms may aid in grasping glandular secretions.

hrp1-male-perineal-pudendal-anatomy.stem: Which landmark is palpated for a pudendal nerve block?
hrp1-male-perineal-pudendal-anatomy.explanation: The pudendal nerve crosses near the ischial spine and sacrospinous ligament.

hrp1-male-perineal-pudendal-anatomy.stem: Regarding pudendal course — which is correct?

options.text: Pudendal nerve remains inside the pelvis to reach perineum
It exits and re-enters through the greater and lesser sciatic foramina
Local anesthetic reaches pudendal nerve near sacrospinous ligament
Pudendal entrapment can occur along its pelvic/perineal course

hrp1-male-perineal-pudendal-anatomy.explanation: The loop around the ischial spine is its defining course.

hrp1-male-perineal-pudendal-anatomy.stem: Which should you review before “Male Pelvis, Perineum & Pudendal Pathway”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-male-perineal-pudendal-anatomy.explanation: Understanding hernias is essential for grasping pelvic anatomy.

hrp1-seminiferous-epithelium-spermatogen.stem: Which process forms the acrosome and flagellum from a spermatid?
hrp1-seminiferous-epithelium-spermatogen.explanation: Spermiogenesis remodels round spermatids into elongated spermatozoa.

hrp1-seminiferous-epithelium-spermatogen.stem: Regarding sperm maturation — which is correct?

options.text: Spermiogenesis is structural remodeling of haploid spermatids
Primary spermatocytes are prominent in seminiferous epithelium

hrp1-seminiferous-epithelium-spermatogen.explanation: Chromosome number does not change during the remodeling phase.

hrp1-seminiferous-epithelium-spermatogen.stem: Which should you review before “Seminiferous Epithelium & Spermatogenesis”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-seminiferous-epithelium-spermatogen.explanation: Gametogenesis in females provides a comparative basis for male spermatogenesis.

hrp1-sertoli-leydig-histology.stem: Which cells form the blood–testis barrier?
hrp1-sertoli-leydig-histology.explanation: Tight junctions between adjacent Sertoli cells divide basal and adluminal compartments.

hrp1-sertoli-leydig-histology.stem: Regarding testosterone therapy — which is correct?

options.text: Exogenous testosterone reliably improves sperm production
It can suppress gonadotropins and intratesticular testosterone, reducing sperm production

hrp1-sertoli-leydig-histology.explanation: Spermatogenesis needs very high local androgen maintained by LH-stimulated Leydig cells.

hrp1-sertoli-leydig-histology.stem: Which should you review before “Sertoli Cells, Leydig Cells & Blood–Testis Barrier”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-sertoli-leydig-histology.explanation: Basic understanding of genetic mechanisms may aid in comprehending cell functions.

hrp1-male-duct-gland-penis-histology.stem: Which histologic feature best identifies vas deferens?
hrp1-male-duct-gland-penis-histology.explanation: The vas deferens has a narrow lumen surrounded by a strikingly thick smooth-muscle wall.

hrp1-male-duct-gland-penis-histology.stem: Regarding epididymal surface — which is correct?

options.text: They are long nonmotile microvilli for absorption and secretion

hrp1-male-duct-gland-penis-histology.explanation: They modify luminal fluid rather than beat to propel sperm.

hrp1-pelvic-diaphragm.stem: Which levator ani component forms a sling around the anorectal junction?
hrp1-pelvic-diaphragm.explanation: Puborectalis maintains the anorectal angle as a muscular sling.

hrp1-pelvic-diaphragm.stem: Regarding pelvic floor — which is correct?

options.text: Pelvic floor must remain maximally contracted during defecation
Puborectalis and sphincters must relax in coordination
Puborectalis sling no longer maintains the continence angle

hrp1-pelvic-diaphragm.explanation: Failure to relax produces outlet dyssynergia.

hrp1-perineal-spaces-triangles.stem: The roots of penis or clitoris lie mainly in which compartment?
hrp1-perineal-spaces-triangles.explanation: Crura and bulbs with their muscles occupy the superficial perineal pouch.

hrp1-perineal-spaces-triangles.stem: Regarding perineal extravasation — which is correct?

options.text: Scarpa/Colles fascia attaches to fascia lata below inguinal ligament and limits thigh spread
Spongy urethral rupture tracks within continuous superficial fascia
Fat-filled fossae communicate around anal canal

hrp1-perineal-spaces-triangles.explanation: Fascial attachments channel rather than randomly disperse fluid.

hrp1-perineal-spaces-triangles.stem: Which should you review before “Perineal Triangles, Fascia & Pouches”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-perineal-spaces-triangles.explanation: Similar fascial concepts apply in neck and perineal regions.

hrp1-pudendal-erectile-external-genitali.stem: Which signaling molecule directly relaxes cavernosal smooth muscle during erection?
hrp1-pudendal-erectile-external-genitali.explanation: Parasympathetic NO increases cGMP and relaxes cavernosal smooth muscle.

hrp1-pudendal-erectile-external-genitali.stem: Regarding erectile innervation — which is correct?

options.text: Pudendal somatic fibers alone initiate cavernosal vasodilation
Parasympathetic cavernous nerves initiate NO-mediated erection
Dorsal genital nerves are terminal pudendal branches

hrp1-pudendal-erectile-external-genitali.explanation: Pudendal pathways supply sensation and striated muscle rather than the primary arterial relaxation signal.

hrp1-pudendal-erectile-external-genitali.stem: Which should you review before “Pudendal Neurovasculature, Erectile Tissues & External Genitalia”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-pudendal-erectile-external-genitali.explanation: Basic understanding of neurovasculature is foundational.

hrp1-sex-steroid-synthesis-action.stem: Which enzyme converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone?
hrp1-sex-steroid-synthesis-action.explanation: 5α-reductase produces the more potent androgen DHT in target tissues.

hrp1-sex-steroid-synthesis-action.stem: Regarding steroid storage — which is correct?

options.text: Gonadal steroids are stored in secretory vesicles
They are synthesized on demand and diffuse out
SHBG concentration alters the bound circulating pool

hrp1-sex-steroid-synthesis-action.explanation: Lipophilic steroids cross membranes and cannot be retained efficiently in ordinary granules.

hrp1-sex-steroid-synthesis-action.stem: Which should you review before “Sex Steroid Synthesis, Transport & Receptor Action”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-sex-steroid-synthesis-action.explanation: Cholesterol is the precursor for sex steroid synthesis.

hrp1-male-hpg-axis.stem: Which hormone directly stimulates Leydig-cell testosterone synthesis?
Regarding gnrh delivery — which is correct?

options.text: Continuous GnRH maintains normal LH/FSH secretion
Pulses stimulate; continuous exposure downregulates the axis

hrp1-male-hpg-axis.explanation: Pituitary GnRH receptors require pulsatile signaling.

hrp1-testosterone-dht-estrogen-actions.stem: Which hormone is most important for male external genital development?
hrp1-testosterone-dht-estrogen-actions.explanation: DHT generated from testosterone drives masculinization of external genitalia and prostate.

hrp1-testosterone-dht-estrogen-actions.stem: Regarding male estrogen — which is correct?

options.text: Estradiol has no important physiologic role in males
Estradiol is essential for male bone maturation and feedback
5α-reductase deficiency reduces DHT but preserves testosterone-mediated Wolffian development
Estradiol is a major male skeletal sex steroid

hrp1-testosterone-dht-estrogen-actions.explanation: Male tissues generate estradiol through aromatization of androgens.

hrp1-estrogen-progesterone-actions.stem: Which hormone transforms proliferative endometrium into secretory endometrium?
hrp1-estrogen-progesterone-actions.explanation: Luteal progesterone prepares the endometrium for implantation.

hrp1-estrogen-progesterone-actions.stem: Regarding endometrial protection — which is correct?

options.text: Unopposed systemic estrogen is harmless with an intact uterus
Chronic unopposed estrogen increases endometrial hyperplasia/cancer risk

hrp1-estrogen-progesterone-actions.explanation: Progesterone normally limits and differentiates estrogen-driven proliferation.

hrp1-normal-puberty-tanner.stem: What is usually the first clinical sign of puberty in boys?
hrp1-normal-puberty-tanner.explanation: Increasing testicular volume is the earliest reliable sign of male gonadarche.

hrp1-normal-puberty-tanner.stem: Regarding puberty onset — which is correct?

options.text: Pubic hair alone proves central puberty
Pubic hair may reflect adrenarche without HPG-axis activation
Central gonadotropin activation stimulates seminiferous tissue
Adrenarche may occur without true central puberty

hrp1-normal-puberty-tanner.explanation: Adrenal and gonadal maturation are related but distinct processes.

hrp1-normal-puberty-tanner.stem: Which should you review before “Normal Puberty, HPG Reactivation & Tanner Staging”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-normal-puberty-tanner.explanation: Basic understanding of viral infections may be helpful.

hrp1-central-precocious-puberty.stem: Which finding supports central rather than peripheral precocious puberty?
hrp1-central-precocious-puberty.explanation: A pubertal gonadotropin response demonstrates central HPG-axis activation.

hrp1-central-precocious-puberty.stem: Regarding gnrh therapy — which is correct?

options.text: A long-acting GnRH agonist continuously stimulates puberty
Continuous exposure downregulates pituitary GnRH receptors
Gonadotropins stimulate both testes in central puberty

hrp1-central-precocious-puberty.explanation: Pulsatile and continuous GnRH have opposite long-term effects.

hrp1-peripheral-precocious-puberty.stem: A virilized young boy has high testosterone, suppressed LH, and one enlarged testis. What is most likely?
hrp1-peripheral-precocious-puberty.explanation: Unilateral enlargement plus suppressed LH points to a local GnRH-independent androgen source.

hrp1-peripheral-precocious-puberty.stem: Regarding precocious puberty treatment — which is correct?

options.text: All cases respond to long-acting GnRH agonist
Peripheral disease requires treatment of its steroid source
Extragonadal androgen suppresses LH/FSH without stimulating seminiferous growth

hrp1-peripheral-precocious-puberty.explanation: The hypothalamic–pituitary axis is already suppressed rather than driving the process.

hrp1-peripheral-precocious-puberty.stem: Which should you review before “Peripheral Precocious Puberty”?

options.text: Humoral Response: B-Cell Activation (T-dependent vs T-independent)
Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-peripheral-precocious-puberty.explanation: Understanding B-cell activation is essential for grasping hormonal interactions in puberty.

hrp1-delayed-puberty.stem: Low estradiol with markedly elevated FSH indicates which pattern?
hrp1-delayed-puberty.explanation: High gonadotropins show that the pituitary is responding to primary gonadal failure.

hrp1-delayed-puberty.stem: Regarding delayed puberty — which is correct?

options.text: All low LH/FSH results indicate permanent pituitary disease
Functional suppression and constitutional delay can also lower gonadotropins
Turner gonadal dysgenesis causes hypergonadotropic hypogonadism

hrp1-delayed-puberty.explanation: Nutrition, chronic illness, exercise, and maturation timing influence the axis.

hrp1-ovarian-steroid-two-cell-model.stem: Which ovarian cell uses FSH-stimulated aromatase?
hrp1-ovarian-steroid-two-cell-model.explanation: Granulosa cells convert theca-derived androgens to estrogens.

hrp1-ovarian-steroid-two-cell-model.stem: Regarding ovarian estrogen synthesis — which is correct?

options.text: Granulosa cells make all androgen substrate de novo under LH alone
Theca supplies androgen; FSH-stimulated granulosa aromatizes it
Theca responds to LH outside avascular granulosa layer
Increasing granulosa mass/aromatase converts theca androgen

hrp1-ovarian-steroid-two-cell-model.explanation: The cooperative two-cell model distributes key enzymes between cell types.

hrp1-cycle-feedback-gonadotropins.stem: What directly triggers the midcycle LH surge?
hrp1-cycle-feedback-gonadotropins.explanation: Sustained high estradiol from the dominant follicle switches to positive feedback.

hrp1-cycle-feedback-gonadotropins.stem: Regarding estrogen feedback — which is correct?

options.text: Sustained high estradiol produces positive feedback and LH surge
Positive estradiol feedback creates midcycle surge
Estradiol/inhibin suppress FSH, eliminating less sensitive follicles

hrp1-cycle-feedback-gonadotropins.explanation: Magnitude and duration determine feedback direction.

hrp1-cycle-feedback-gonadotropins.stem: Which should you review before “GnRH, FSH/LH Feedback & the Midcycle Surge”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-cycle-feedback-gonadotropins.explanation: Understanding feedback mechanisms is essential for grasping hormonal regulation.

hrp1-ovarian-cycle-ovulation.stem: Which ovarian structure is the main progesterone source after ovulation?
hrp1-ovarian-cycle-ovulation.explanation: Luteinized granulosa/theca cells in corpus luteum produce progesterone.

hrp1-ovarian-cycle-ovulation.stem: Regarding cycle timing — which is correct?

options.text: Luteal phase varies more than follicular phase
Follicular phase accounts for most cycle-length variation
Follicular rupture can cause brief unilateral pain

hrp1-ovarian-cycle-ovulation.explanation: Corpus-luteum lifespan is relatively consistent without pregnancy.

hrp1-uterine-cycle-fertility-signs.stem: Which change occurs after ovulation under progesterone?
hrp1-uterine-cycle-fertility-signs.explanation: Progesterone thickens cervical mucus and raises basal body temperature.

hrp1-uterine-cycle-fertility-signs.stem: Regarding ovulation testing — which is correct?

options.text: A positive LH kit proves successful ovulation
It predicts a surge; follicle rupture may still fail
Estrogen-rich preovulatory state increases salt/water content

hrp1-uterine-cycle-fertility-signs.explanation: LH signaling can occur without actual oocyte release.

hrp1-uterine-cycle-fertility-signs.stem: Which should you review before “Uterine Cycle, Ovulation Signs & Hormonal Contraception”?

options.text: Uterine Tubes, Ovaries, Lymphatics & Clinical Anatomy

hrp1-placenta-endocrine-hcg.stem: What is the principal early-pregnancy action of hCG?
hrp1-placenta-endocrine-hcg.explanation: hCG stimulates luteal LH receptors so progesterone production continues.

hrp1-placenta-endocrine-hcg.stem: Regarding pregnancy diagnosis — which is correct?

options.text: A positive hCG proves an intrauterine pregnancy
It proves trophoblastic hormone production, not pregnancy location
hCG secretion begins soon after implantation
Pregnancy location or viability may be abnormal

hrp1-placenta-endocrine-hcg.explanation: Ectopic pregnancy and trophoblastic disease can also produce hCG.

bone-biology-remodeling.stem: Which molecule, produced by osteoblasts, acts as a decoy receptor that binds RANKL and thereby inhibits osteoclast activation?

bone-biology-remodeling.stem: Regarding rankl vs opg — which is correct?

options.text: Osteoprotegerin (OPG) activates osteoclasts to increase bone resorption

metabolic-bone-disease.stem: Regarding osteoporosis vs osteomalacia — which is correct?

metabolic-bone-disease.explanation: The two differ in mechanism — osteoporosis is a mass problem with normal mineral content, whereas osteomalacia/rickets is a mineralization defect — which changes the workup (DXA vs vitamin D/PTH).

metabolic-bone-disease.stem: What best explains the finding: “Fragility fracture with normal calcium/phosphate”?

metabolic-bone-disease.explanation: Bowed legs + rachitic rosary in a child → Rickets (vitamin D deficiency).

osteomyelitis-avn-paget.stem: An older patient has an enlarging skull, progressive hearing loss, bowed legs, and a markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium. Bone shows a mosaic lamellar pattern. The diagnosis is:
osteomyelitis-avn-paget.explanation: Paget disease (osteitis deformans) produces disordered high-turnover bone (mosaic lamellar pattern), enlarged skull with cotton-wool appearance, cranial-nerve compression, and a very high alkaline phosphatase with normal calcium.

osteomyelitis-avn-paget.stem: Regarding osteomyelitis organism in sickle cell disease — which is correct?

options.text: Osteomyelitis in a sickle-cell patient is caused by Staphylococcus aureus like most cases
While S. aureus is the overall most common cause, Salmonella is characteristically associated with osteomyelitis in sickle-cell disease

osteomyelitis-avn-paget.explanation: Sickle-cell patients have a distinctive predisposition to Salmonella osteomyelitis — a classic exam association even though S. aureus dominates in the general population.

osteomyelitis-avn-paget.stem: What best explains the finding: “Sequestrum + involucrum on imaging/histology”?
osteomyelitis-avn-paget.explanation: Sequestrum + involucrum on imaging/histology → Chronic pyogenic osteomyelitis.

osteomyelitis-avn-paget.stem: What best explains the finding: “Empty osteocyte lacunae”?
osteomyelitis-avn-paget.explanation: Empty osteocyte lacunae → Avascular necrosis (dead bone).

osteomyelitis-avn-paget.stem: Which should you review before “Osteomyelitis, AVN & Paget Disease”?

options.text: Plasma Membrane: Fluid Mosaic, Glycocalyx & Transport

osteomyelitis-avn-paget.explanation: Basic understanding of membrane transport is helpful for understanding bone pathology.

neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.stem: A 5-year-old boy has proximal weakness, uses his hands to “climb up” his legs when standing (Gowers sign), has enlarged calves, and a very high creatine kinase. The most likely diagnosis is:
neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.explanation: X-linked Duchenne muscular dystrophy (absent dystrophin) presents around age 5 with proximal weakness, Gowers sign, calf pseudohypertrophy, and a markedly elevated CK.

neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.stem: Regarding calf enlargement in duchenne — which is correct?

options.text: Enlarged calves in Duchenne muscular dystrophy indicate strong, hypertrophied muscle
It is PSEUDOhypertrophy — the calf is enlarged by fatty and fibrous replacement of degenerated muscle, not by true muscle growth

neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.explanation: The bulky calf is weak because functional muscle is being lost and replaced by fat/fibrosis, a hallmark of Duchenne.

neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.stem: What best explains the finding: “Gowers sign + calf pseudohypertrophy in a boy”?
neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.explanation: Gowers sign + calf pseudohypertrophy in a boy → Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.stem: What best explains the finding: “Fiber-type grouping / grouped atrophy”?
neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.explanation: Fiber-type grouping / grouped atrophy → Denervation and reinnervation.

neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.stem: Which is a clinical application of “Neurogenic Atrophy & Muscular Dystrophy”?
neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.explanation: Neurogenic conditions can affect both muscle and bladder function.

neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.stem: Which should you review before “Neurogenic Atrophy & Muscular Dystrophy”?
neurogenic-muscular-dystrophy.explanation: Understanding atrophy mechanisms is crucial for neurogenic atrophy.

inflammatory-myopathies.stem: A patient on a statin develops progressive proximal weakness and a very high CK that does NOT improve after stopping the statin; biopsy shows necrotic fibers with membrane-attack complex on the sarcolemma. The diagnosis is:
inflammatory-myopathies.explanation: Persistent necrotizing myopathy after statin withdrawal, with MAC on the sarcolemma and anti-HMGCR antibodies, is immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy — it requires immunosuppression, unlike self-limited statin myalgia.

inflammatory-myopathies.stem: Regarding adult-onset dermatomyositis — which is correct?

options.text: Adult dermatomyositis just needs immunosuppression like the childhood form
In adults, dermatomyositis is frequently paraneoplastic — an age-appropriate malignancy screen is essential

inflammatory-myopathies.explanation: DM in adults is strongly associated with occult cancer, so missing the malignancy work-up can delay a critical diagnosis.

inflammatory-myopathies.stem: What best explains the finding: “Heliotrope rash + Gottron papules + proximal weakness”?
inflammatory-myopathies.explanation: Heliotrope rash + Gottron papules + proximal weakness → Dermatomyositis.

inflammatory-myopathies.stem: What best explains the finding: “Statin-associated myopathy that persists after stopping the statin”?
inflammatory-myopathies.explanation: Statin-associated myopathy that persists after stopping the statin → Anti-HMGCR necrotizing myopathy.

inflammatory-myopathies.stem: Which should you review before “Inflammatory Myopathies”?
inflammatory-myopathies.explanation: Understanding muscle contraction is essential for grasping myopathy mechanisms.

metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.stem: A smoker develops proximal leg weakness and dry mouth; strength briefly improves after sustained contraction, and cholinesterase inhibitors give little benefit. Antibodies target the presynaptic calcium channel. The diagnosis and key association are:

options.text: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome; small-cell lung cancer

metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.explanation: LEMS is caused by antibodies to presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels, is paraneoplastic (classically small-cell lung cancer), improves with repeated use, and responds poorly to cholinesterase inhibitors.

metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.stem: Regarding mg vs lems response pattern — which is correct?

options.text: Both myasthenia gravis and LEMS improve with cholinesterase inhibitors and worsen with sustained activity
MG (postsynaptic) FATIGUES with use and improves with cholinesterase inhibitors; LEMS (presynaptic) IMPROVES with repeated use and responds poorly to cholinesterase inhibitors

metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.explanation: The site of the lesion flips the pattern — postsynaptic receptor loss fatigues, while presynaptic calcium-channel blockade improves as repeated firing builds up calcium and ACh release.

metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.stem: What best explains the finding: “Fatigable ptosis/diplopia worsening through the day”?
metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.explanation: Fatigable ptosis/diplopia worsening through the day → Myasthenia gravis (postsynaptic AChR).

metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.stem: What best explains the finding: “Proximal weakness improving with repeated effort + dry mouth”?
metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.explanation: Proximal weakness improving with repeated effort + dry mouth → LEMS (presynaptic Ca channel).

metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.stem: Which should you review before “Metabolic, Toxic & Neuromuscular-Junction Disorders”?
metabolic-toxic-nmj-myopathy.explanation: Knowledge of energy systems is crucial for metabolic myopathies.

joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.stem: A hot, swollen knee is aspirated; synovial fluid shows 80,000 WBC/mm³ with 90% neutrophils. The most concerning diagnosis is:
joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.explanation: A synovial WBC count >50,000 with a neutrophil predominance (>75%) indicates septic arthritis — a joint emergency requiring urgent drainage and antibiotics.

joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.stem: Regarding why cartilage heals poorly — which is correct?

options.text: Articular cartilage heals well because it is bathed in nutrient-rich synovial fluid
Hyaline articular cartilage is avascular and aneural, so it has limited capacity to regenerate after injury

joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.explanation: Lacking blood supply, cartilage depends on slow diffusion from synovial fluid and cannot mount an effective repair — a key reason osteoarthritis progresses.

joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.stem: What best explains the finding: “Cloudy joint fluid, WBC >50,000, >75% PMN”?
joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.explanation: Cloudy joint fluid, WBC >50,000, >75% PMN → Septic (bacterial) arthritis.

joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.stem: What best explains the finding: “Clear, viscous fluid, WBC <2,000”?
joint-anatomy-synovial-fluid.explanation: Clear, viscous fluid, WBC <2,000 → Non-inflammatory (e.g. osteoarthritis).

osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.stem: A 45-year-old woman has symmetric swelling of the MCP and PIP joints, more than an hour of morning stiffness, subcutaneous nodules, and positive anti-CCP antibodies. The diagnosis is:
osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.explanation: Symmetric small-joint (MCP/PIP) synovitis with prolonged morning stiffness, rheumatoid nodules, and positive anti-CCP (ACPA) is rheumatoid arthritis — an autoimmune, pannus-forming arthritis.

osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.stem: Regarding dip involvement oa vs ra — which is correct?

options.text: Rheumatoid arthritis characteristically involves the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joints
RA typically SPARES the DIP joints (favoring MCP/PIP); DIP involvement (Heberden nodes) is characteristic of osteoarthritis

osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.explanation: The joint distribution is a key discriminator — DIP nodes point to OA, while RA is a symmetric MCP/PIP synovitis, so mislabeling DIP disease as RA is a classic error.

osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.stem: What best explains the finding: “Heberden (DIP) and Bouchard (PIP) nodes, worse with use”?
osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.explanation: Heberden (DIP) and Bouchard (PIP) nodes, worse with use → Osteoarthritis.

osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.stem: What best explains the finding: “Symmetric MCP/PIP swelling, >1 h morning stiffness, swan-neck”?
osteoarthritis-rheumatoid.explanation: Symmetric MCP/PIP swelling, >1 h morning stiffness, swan-neck → Rheumatoid arthritis.

spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.stem: Aspiration of an acutely inflamed first metatarsophalangeal joint shows needle-shaped crystals that are negatively birefringent under polarized light. The diagnosis is:
spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.explanation: Needle-shaped, negatively birefringent monosodium urate crystals in a painful first MTP joint (podagra) are diagnostic of gout; pseudogout shows rhomboid, positively birefringent CPPD crystals.

spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.stem: Regarding crystal birefringence — which is correct?

options.text: Positively birefringent needle-shaped crystals indicate gout
Gout = NEEDLE-shaped, NEGATIVELY birefringent (MSU); pseudogout = RHOMBOID, POSITIVELY birefringent (CPPD)

spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.explanation: Swapping the shape/birefringence is a classic exam trap — needle + negative = gout, rhomboid + positive = pseudogout.

spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.stem: What best explains the finding: “Young man, inflammatory back pain, bamboo spine, HLA-B27”?
spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.explanation: Young man, inflammatory back pain, bamboo spine, HLA-B27 → Ankylosing spondylitis.

spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.stem: What best explains the finding: “Acute painful first MTP + needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals”?
spondyloarthropathies-crystal-arthritis.explanation: Acute painful first MTP + needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals → Gout.

cox-pathway-nsaids.stem: Why does low-dose aspirin provide long-lasting antiplatelet effect while ibuprofen does not?

options.text: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1, which platelets cannot resynthesize (no nucleus)
Ibuprofen is a stronger COX inhibitor

cox-pathway-nsaids.explanation: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates COX-1; because platelets are anucleate and cannot make new enzyme, thromboxane A₂ is suppressed for the platelet lifespan (7–10 days). Reversible NSAIDs like ibuprofen wear off as the drug clears.

cox-pathway-nsaids.stem: Regarding why coxibs increase cardiovascular risk — which is correct?

options.text: COX-2 inhibitors are cardioprotective like low-dose aspirin because they reduce inflammation
Coxibs block endothelial COX-2 (PGI₂, anti-clotting) while sparing platelet COX-1 (TXA₂, pro-clotting), shifting the balance toward thrombosis and RAISING cardiovascular risk

cox-pathway-nsaids.explanation: Unlike aspirin’s antiplatelet effect, selective COX-2 inhibition removes the protective prostacyclin without touching platelet thromboxane — tipping toward clotting.

cox-pathway-nsaids.stem: What best explains the finding: “Low-dose aspirin prevents MI/stroke”?
cox-pathway-nsaids.explanation: Low-dose aspirin prevents MI/stroke → Irreversible platelet COX-1 → ↓ TXA₂.

cox-pathway-nsaids.stem: What best explains the finding: “Coxib with lower GI bleeding but higher MI risk”?
cox-pathway-nsaids.explanation: Coxib with lower GI bleeding but higher MI risk → Spare COX-1; block endothelial PGI₂.

nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.stem: A patient with a large paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose is at risk of hepatotoxicity from the toxic metabolite NAPQI. The specific antidote is:
nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.explanation: N-acetylcysteine replenishes hepatic glutathione, allowing detoxification of NAPQI, and is the specific antidote for acetaminophen (paracetamol) overdose.

nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.stem: Regarding acetaminophen in inflammatory disease — which is correct?

options.text: Acetaminophen can replace NSAIDs for the inflammation of rheumatoid arthritis
Acetaminophen has minimal anti-inflammatory activity (works only where peroxide levels are low), so it relieves pain/fever but is not an adequate substitute for NSAIDs in inflammatory joint disease

nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.explanation: In inflamed tissue, high peroxide levels neutralize acetaminophen’s COX inhibition, so it does not control inflammation the way NSAIDs do.

nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.stem: What best explains the finding: “AKI after starting an NSAID with ACEi + diuretic”?
nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.explanation: AKI after starting an NSAID with ACEi + diuretic → Triple whammy.

nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.stem: What best explains the finding: “Encephalopathy + hepatic dysfunction in a child given aspirin”?
nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.explanation: Encephalopathy + hepatic dysfunction in a child given aspirin → Reye syndrome.

nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.stem: Which should you review before “NSAID Safety & Acetaminophen”?
nsaid-acetaminophen-safety.explanation: Understanding acetaminophen overdose is crucial for recognizing toxicity.

rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.stem: Which is the first-line disease-modifying drug for rheumatoid arthritis, acting by inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase?
rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.explanation: Methotrexate, a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor that suppresses lymphocyte proliferation, is the first-line DMARD for rheumatoid arthritis (contraindicated in pregnancy; monitor liver and marrow).

rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.stem: Regarding before starting a tnf inhibitor — which is correct?

options.text: Biologic DMARDs can be started immediately once conventional DMARDs fail
Screen for latent tuberculosis (and hepatitis) before starting a TNF inhibitor, because TNF blockade can reactivate TB

rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.explanation: TNF is essential for granuloma maintenance, so blocking it can reactivate latent TB — screening is mandatory before anti-TNF therapy.

rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.stem: What best explains the finding: “Reactivation of latent TB on a biologic”?
rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.explanation: Reactivation of latent TB on a biologic → TNF blockade.

rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.stem: What best explains the finding: “Retinopathy on a long-term DMARD”?
rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.explanation: Retinopathy on a long-term DMARD → Hydroxychloroquine.

rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.stem: Which should you review before “Rheumatoid Arthritis Drugs (DMARDs)”?
rheumatoid-arthritis-drugs.explanation: Understanding nucleotide metabolism is foundational for drug mechanisms.

gout-drugs.stem: Before starting allopurinol in a Thai patient with chronic gout, which test reduces the risk of a severe cutaneous reaction (SJS/TEN)?
gout-drugs.explanation: The HLA-B*58:01 allele (common in Southeast Asians) strongly predicts allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome (SJS/TEN), so screening is recommended before starting allopurinol.

gout-drugs.stem: Regarding aspirin in gout — which is correct?

options.text: Aspirin is a good NSAID choice for an acute gout flare
Avoid aspirin in gout — low-dose aspirin causes urate RETENTION and can worsen it; use indomethacin/naproxen, colchicine, or steroids instead

gout-drugs.explanation: Aspirin has dose-dependent effects on urate handling (low dose retains urate), so it is specifically excluded from the acute-gout NSAID options.

gout-drugs.stem: What best explains the finding: “Bloody diarrhea after gout medication”?
gout-drugs.explanation: Bloody diarrhea after gout medication → Colchicine toxicity.

gout-drugs.stem: What best explains the finding: “Severe cutaneous reaction (SJS/TEN) on urate-lowering drug”?
gout-drugs.explanation: Severe cutaneous reaction (SJS/TEN) on urate-lowering drug → Allopurinol hypersensitivity (HLA-B*58:01).

gout-drugs.stem: Which should you review before “Gout Drugs”?
gout-drugs.explanation: Understanding nucleotide degradation is essential for grasping gout pathophysiology.

rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.stem: A 25-year-old athlete has an acute lateral ankle sprain 18 hours ago with significant swelling. The most appropriate physical modality now is:
rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.explanation: In the acute phase (first 24–48 h), cold therapy reduces blood flow, metabolism, and inflammation; heat and vigorous massage would worsen the acute swelling.

rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.stem: Regarding modality for an acute injury — which is correct?

options.text: Apply heat to a freshly sprained ankle to relax it and ease pain
Use COLD (cryotherapy) in the acute phase (first 24–48 h) — heat increases blood flow and worsens swelling/inflammation early on
Increased blood flow and tissue extensibility

rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.explanation: Acute injuries are inflammatory; heat’s vasodilation aggravates edema, whereas cold’s vasoconstriction limits it — so heat is reserved for chronic stages.

rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.stem: What best explains the finding: “Acute ankle sprain within 48 h → apply cold”?

options.text: Increased blood flow and tissue extensibility

rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.explanation: Acute ankle sprain within 48 h → apply cold → Vasoconstriction limits swelling/inflammation.

rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.stem: What best explains the finding: “Chronic stiff arthritic joint → apply heat”?

options.text: Increased blood flow and tissue extensibility

rehab-thermotherapy-electrotherapy.explanation: Chronic stiff arthritic joint → apply heat → Increased blood flow and tissue extensibility.

rehab-modalities-selection.stem: A tibial shaft fracture shows no callus and a persistent gap 7 months after casting (established non-union), with no infection or nearby metal implant. Which physical modality has the strongest evidence base?
rehab-modalities-selection.explanation: PEMF is FDA-approved for non-union and delayed-union fractures; it induces osteoblast activity and angiogenesis to promote bone healing.

rehab-modalities-selection.stem: Regarding traction in inflammatory spondyloarthropathy — which is correct?

options.text: Spinal traction is helpful for back stiffness in ankylosing spondylitis
Traction is CONTRAINDICATED in ankylosing spondylitis (and osteoporosis) — the inflamed, ossified, fragile spine can be injured

rehab-modalities-selection.explanation: The rigid, brittle, fused spine of AS (and low-density bone in osteoporosis) is at risk of fracture with distraction forces, so traction is avoided.

rehab-modalities-selection.stem: What best explains the finding: “Established non-union fracture”?
rehab-modalities-selection.explanation: Established non-union fracture → PEMF (FDA-approved) stimulates osteogenesis.

rehab-modalities-selection.stem: What best explains the finding: “Recalcitrant calcific supraspinatus tendinitis”?
rehab-modalities-selection.explanation: Recalcitrant calcific supraspinatus tendinitis → ESWT (best evidence).

rehab-modalities-selection.stem: Which should you review before “Traction, Shockwave & Modality Selection”?

calcium-homeostasis-hormones.stem: Teriparatide (a PTH analog) builds bone in osteoporosis, whereas chronic hyperparathyroidism destroys bone. The explanation is that:

options.text: Teriparatide is not actually a form of PTH
Intermittent low-dose PTH stimulates osteoblasts (formation), while continuous high PTH stimulates osteoclasts (resorption)
PTH only acts on the kidney

calcium-homeostasis-hormones.explanation: PTH has a dose-dependent effect on bone: intermittent low doses favor osteoblastic bone formation (teriparatide’s anabolic action), while sustained high levels drive osteoclastic resorption.

calcium-homeostasis-hormones.stem: Regarding dose-dependent pth effect — which is correct?

options.text: PTH always breaks down bone, so a PTH drug could never treat osteoporosis
PTH is dose-dependent: continuous high levels resorb bone, but INTERMITTENT low-dose PTH (teriparatide) stimulates osteoblasts and BUILDS bone

calcium-homeostasis-hormones.explanation: The paradox is central to bone pharmacology — pulsed PTH is anabolic, which is why teriparatide is given as a once-daily injection to increase bone formation.

calcium-homeostasis-hormones.stem: What best explains the finding: “Rising serum calcium with high PTH”?
calcium-homeostasis-hormones.explanation: Rising serum calcium with high PTH → PTH mobilizes bone + renal/gut calcium.

calcium-homeostasis-hormones.stem: What best explains the finding: “Bone formation from intermittent low-dose PTH”?
calcium-homeostasis-hormones.explanation: Bone formation from intermittent low-dose PTH → Osteoblast stimulation (teriparatide).

calcium-homeostasis-hormones.stem: Which should you review before “Calcium Homeostasis & Bone Hormones”?
calcium-homeostasis-hormones.explanation: Calcitonin's role in calcium homeostasis is directly related.

osteoporosis-drugs.stem: A postmenopausal woman with osteoporosis is started on the first-line drug class that induces osteoclast apoptosis. She must take it on an empty stomach and stay upright afterward. This drug class is:
osteoporosis-drugs.explanation: Bisphosphonates are first-line antiresorptives that trigger osteoclast apoptosis; oral forms are poorly absorbed and irritant, so they are taken fasting with the patient remaining upright to prevent esophagitis.

osteoporosis-drugs.stem: Regarding how to take oral bisphosphonates — which is correct?

options.text: Oral bisphosphonates can be taken with food and lying down like most tablets
Take oral bisphosphonates on an empty stomach with water and remain UPRIGHT for 30–60 minutes — they are poorly absorbed and cause esophagitis

osteoporosis-drugs.explanation: Poor oral bioavailability and mucosal irritation mean food blocks absorption and reclining risks esophagitis, so the fasting/upright rule is essential.

osteoporosis-drugs.stem: What best explains the finding: “Non-healing jaw wound after dental work on bone therapy”?
osteoporosis-drugs.explanation: Non-healing jaw wound after dental work on bone therapy → Osteonecrosis of the jaw (bisphosphonate/denosumab).

osteoporosis-drugs.stem: What best explains the finding: “Atypical subtrochanteric femoral fracture”?
osteoporosis-drugs.explanation: Atypical subtrochanteric femoral fracture → Long-term bisphosphonate.

tumor-classification-grading.stem: For soft-tissue sarcomas, which grading system — based on tumor differentiation, mitotic count, and necrosis — is the most important predictor of prognosis and metastatic risk?
tumor-classification-grading.explanation: The FNCLCC system grades soft-tissue sarcomas (grade 1–3) using tumor differentiation, mitotic count, and percentage necrosis — the key determinant of prognosis and need for adjuvant therapy.

tumor-classification-grading.stem: Regarding intermediate tumor behavior — which is correct?

options.text: A locally aggressive, recurring tumor must be malignant and will metastasize
Intermediate tumors (e.g. desmoid fibromatosis) are locally aggressive and recur but rarely or never metastasize — distinct from malignant sarcomas

tumor-classification-grading.explanation: Local aggressiveness alone does not equal malignancy; the intermediate category captures tumors that invade/recur locally without significant metastatic potential.

tumor-classification-grading.stem: What best explains the finding: “Locally aggressive tumor that recurs but rarely spreads”?
tumor-classification-grading.explanation: Locally aggressive tumor that recurs but rarely spreads → Intermediate (e.g. desmoid fibromatosis).

tumor-classification-grading.stem: What best explains the finding: “High mitotic count + necrosis on biopsy”?
tumor-classification-grading.explanation: High mitotic count + necrosis on biopsy → High FNCLCC grade → worse prognosis.

tumor-classification-grading.stem: Which should you review before “MSK Tumor Classification & Grading”?
tumor-classification-grading.explanation: Differentiation and invasion are key in distinguishing tumor behavior.

soft-tissue-tumors.stem: A 6-year-old presents with a soft-tissue mass; biopsy shows primitive cells with occasional cross-striated rhabdomyoblasts. The diagnosis is:
soft-tissue-tumors.explanation: Rhabdomyosarcoma, the most common childhood soft-tissue sarcoma, is diagnosed by rhabdomyoblasts (skeletal-muscle differentiation, sometimes with cross-striations); the embryonal subtype is most common.

soft-tissue-tumors.stem: Regarding most common childhood soft-tissue sarcoma — which is correct?

options.text: The most common soft-tissue sarcoma in children is liposarcoma
Rhabdomyosarcoma is the most common soft-tissue sarcoma in children; liposarcoma occurs mostly in adults

soft-tissue-tumors.explanation: Age matters — rhabdomyosarcoma (rhabdomyoblasts) dominates in children/teens, whereas liposarcoma is an adult sarcoma.

soft-tissue-tumors.stem: What best explains the finding: “Child with a soft-tissue mass containing rhabdomyoblasts”?
soft-tissue-tumors.explanation: Child with a soft-tissue mass containing rhabdomyoblasts → Rhabdomyosarcoma.

soft-tissue-tumors.stem: What best explains the finding: “Malignant nerve-sheath tumor in an NF1 patient”?
